thread:
harper-sre: Planning a rolling kernel patch across AZs next Mon 01:00-03:30 UTC. Scope: infra nodes in az-a/az-b/az-c (control-plane + serving). Fixes a network driver regression that can cause transient packet drops. Expect brief connection resets during reboots; p99 serving may spike up to ~4m per AZ. Dedicated customer pools excluded.

devin-sre: Staggered or parallel?

harper-sre: Staggered. Plan: patch az-a, wait 30m, then az-b, wait 30m, then az-c. We'll cordon+drain one node at a time and prewarm standby nodes to reduce cold starts.

maya-oncall: I'll be primary for the window. What's the exact rollback if things go sideways?

harper-sre: Rollback options: 1) stop maintenance and re-open drained nodes to traffic (`redwoodctl maintenance abort --id kernel-2001234567`). 2) if node instability, reprovision from latest healthy image. 3) route-level revert: set weights back to primaries. I'll paste runbook snippet in #eng-oncall.

alex-platform: I'll apply autoscaler hold: `redwoodctl autoscaler hold --duration 45m` to avoid downscale churn during the patch. Also prewarm 3 standby nodes per AZ.

ops-bot: Maintenance task "kernel-patch-2001234567" created -> Mon 2001234567T01:00:00Z. Notifications sent to #eng-sre and oncall.

harper-sre: Alerts to watch: node.restarts, serving.p95, serving.p99, network.packet_loss, controlplane.replica_lag. Suppress non-actionable noise with `alertctl suppress --tag kernel-patch-2001234567 --until 2001234890`. Critical alerts still fire.

maya-oncall: I'll be at my desk at 00:45 UTC for prechecks. Please @me on any immediate rollbacks.

harper-sre: Expected post-run: short p99 bumps (~20%) for 2-4m during each AZ's drain, no customer routes affected. Abort threshold: >15m sustained degradation in any AZ or any unexpected node restarts.

ops-bot: Maintenance "kernel-patch-2001234567" started (01:00 UTC).

devin-sre: az-a patch complete, p99 spike ~3m then recovered, no restarts. Proceeding to az-b.

harper-sre: az-b patch in progress.

ops-bot: Maintenance "kernel-patch-2001234567" completed (02:58 UTC). Summary: staged rebooted nodes, transient p99 bumps per AZ, no node restarts, packet loss within expected limits. Full postmortem in #eng-sre/postmortems.

maya-oncall: Post-run note: prewarm reduced cold-start tail; recommend same approach for future kernel cycles.

harper-sre: Thanks team. I'll update the SRE calendar and runbook with lessons learned.
